What this changes, and what remains openThis refutes reserve monotonicity from the genuine least marked hull, including when:both the hull and the full fusion are endpoint-connected;every positive owner and every actual marked witness is retained;one additional negative owner generates the entire extension under exact feasible closure;the added owners are not feasible without an existing hull owner.It also rules out a bound on reserve loss depending only on the positive demand, the number of added owners and their original negative mass. In this family those quantities stay fixed at
$$n_2-n_0=1,\qquad 5\text{ added owners},\qquad S_{\rm added}=17,$$
while
$$R(\mathcal H_k)-R(\mathcal J_k)=\frac{k}{2}-11\longrightarrow\infty.$$
A positive fixed fraction of the hull’s reserve or surplus need not survive either.The remaining viable bridge must account for the existing hull margin. Here the exact loss is
$$R(\mathcal H_k)-R(\mathcal J_k)
=\mu(\mathcal H_k)-23.$$
Thus this family permits almost all of an arbitrarily large hull margin to disappear, but leaves  $23$ .The unresolved global step is to prove, with nonreused actual capacities, that such signed losses can never exceed the available allocation margin—or to find a complete fusion where they do. The construction supplies no contradiction to
$$\mu=N+R-G\ge0.$$
The full unrestricted allocation and the rectangular-grid triple equality remain open.
